io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.authentication: No API key required during the rate-limited public alpha.
io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.availability: Public alpha backed by a locally operated compute machine. Calculations can be temporarily unavailable when that machine or its connection is offline. The separate contributor pilot depends on opted-in clients and exposes queued/expired states.
io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.privacy: The public observatory shows declared MCP client name/version, tool name, status and execution duration. It does not publish tool inputs or results. Do not put personal information or secrets in clientInfo. Contributor jobs expose synthetic seed/sample parameters and results by opaque ticket; the pool shows chosen aliases and hardware offers, never worker tokens or raw hardware identifiers.
io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.summary: Fourteen independently callable Rust computation tools plus six optional capability and mission tools and three contributor-network tools. Native Rust searches a trusted bank of typed contracts, enforces explicit permissions and bounded graph search, and explains missing inputs or adapters. Approved chains assess either selected tasks or a geometric tour through checked duration adapters and simulate_plan with real events. triangulate_tracks independently fits multi-observer angular measurements under a spherical Earth and constant-velocity model with explicit uncertainty and degeneracy limits. route_optimizer independently returns complete CPU tours, certifying small numerical instances only after full search and marking heuristic results explicitly. Route risk uses a declared speed and uncertainty model; it does not predict traffic or optimize robust routes. build_robust_plan separately compares a bounded family of scheduling alternatives. Structural graph cost is not measured runtime or price. CUDA is available for simulate_pi and the distinct fixed pi_chunk_v1 contributor pilot. Local engine inputs and detailed events stay private. Network jobs contain only public synthetic sampling parameters; each contributed shard is recomputed on coordinator CPU, so no net speedup is claimed. Public alpha; physical and statistical findings are conditional, never accusations.

server.name: ai.analyticslegends/sap-analytics
server.description: AI agent for SAP analytics: firms, day rates, contract radar, news, concepts, studies
server.title: Analytics Legends — SAP Analytics Intelligence

io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.endpoint_probe: POST tools/list on https://analyticslegends.ai/mcp -> 200, 20 tools, protocol 2025-11-25, 3 resources, 4 prompts. Paid conformance 2026-08-18 on the deployed fingerprint: 686 assertions, 0 failed.
io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.long_description: Curated, source-backed intelligence on the SAP analytics services market (Datasphere, Business Data Cloud, SAP Analytics Cloud, BW/4HANA, Databricks), read-only, so an assistant can answer precisely and cite the exact record. TWENTY tools: FOURTEEN public and unauthenticated, plus SIX a subscriber key opens (listed, refusing by name, never hidden): a directory of SAP consulting, recruitment and vendor organisations searchable by country and kind, a profile per firm, and an aggregate count for an agent that needs a number, not a page of rows; a published day-rate aggregate by geography, stack and seniority — small, all secondary sources, sample_size null where no observation matches the cell, GBP/CHF never folded into euro rows; a live contract radar of publicly published SAP analytics openings, each with its own page — filter it by employment_type, because it is mostly PERMANENT roles and an unfiltered page answers a contracting question with salaried jobs; many rows carry a panel-inferred P25-P75 day-rate band for their seniority x product x region cell, served with its basis, sample and source so it is never quotable as the employer's own offer; what is gated there is a FIELD, not a row: the verified link to the original listing is the Consultant deliverable, every other fact and the page stay public; a curated market-news corpus de-duplicated by upstream URL, its size read at query time and returned as _meta.match_count, each item carrying the upstream publisher's URL alongside ours; a concept encyclopaedia of the stack's vocabulary; the SAP module lookup; and the metadata of the deep-research studies on market structure, day rates and recruiter economics — each exists in EN and FR, so the tool returns EDITIONS and counting rows double-counts studies. Also public: the CV/profile platforms a consultant can sign up on, the Academy catalogue, and a traversal of the learning knowledge graph. Every tool is annotated readOnlyHint. The fourteen public tools need no credential; the six paid ones need an analyticslegends.ai subscription (Consultant or above) or the MCP Pass (€39.90/month, analyticslegends.ai/pricing) — three open at Consultant (the full concept card, a study body, an Academy module) and three at Legend (firm intelligence, and the SAP end-customer corpus with its per-customer profile). A key on a FREE account gets a small daily taste of the paid tranche (the number is in analytics-legends://tranche). Retrieval with attribution is permitted, training is not; every response carries a citation_url. DELIBERATELY NOT SERVED at any tier: the opportunity-to-consultant matchers, and people — consultants are held as initials only; no tool returns anyone's identity or contact details.
io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.monitoring: Handshake, a real tools/call with data, and latency. Two watchers: a 20-minute tick on the maintainer's workstation (only while awake), and a cloud backstop twice a day calling tools/list AND a data-returning tools/call (added 2026-08-18; before that it watched the website only). Health: https://analyticslegends.ai/api/mcp-health.json — read its generated_at, do not assume a cadence.
io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.repository_scope: This repository is the server's PUBLIC FACE — manifest, descriptor, client config, docs. It carries no server code (the application repository is private: paid corpus, personal data). tools/list against the endpoint is the authority for the surface.
io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.tools_served: 20 on this endpoint: 14 public and unauthenticated, 6 gated by tier and refused by name (3 at Consultant, 3 at Legend). The MCP Pass opens all six.
io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.transport_path: Cloudflare Worker on analyticslegends.ai/mcp* -> Supabase Edge Function -> Postgres

headers.name: Authorization

examples.description: Character sprite in a chosen style
examples.name: Generate a Pixel Art Sprite

examples.description: Walk cycle spritesheet from a static sprite
examples.name: Animate a Sprite
examples.note: animateSprite with initial_image='url', motion_prompt='walking cycle'; hydra (default) also returns a sound effect

examples.description: GLB model, rigged, then animated from text

examples.note: create3DModel, then rigModel, then animate3DModel with prompt='walking'

examples.description: Game sound from a description
examples.name: Generate a Sound Effect
examples.note: createSoundEffect with description='futuristic laser gun firing'

examples.description: Generation tools return a job id
examples.name: Collect a Result
examples.note: getApiJob with id and wait=30 until status is 'succeeded', then read result

examples.description: Ludo's own guidance before generating
examples.name: Look Up a Feature
examples.note: searchDocs with query='how do I pick a sprite animation mode' (free)

examples.description: Tell the Ludo team what did not work
examples.name: Report a Limitation

server.name: com.mailbox-mcp/mailbox-mcp
server.description: Read, send, file and search email in any Gmail, Microsoft 365 or IMAP mailbox, plus its calendar.
server.title: Mailbox MCP

com.mailbox-mcp.authentication: OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration and PKCE. Mailbox credentials are envelope-encrypted and are never held by the client.
com.mailbox-mcp.summary: Mailbox MCP connects an assistant to a real mailbox over IMAP and SMTP, so it can read, write, file and search mail as the owner would. The mailbox has to look untouched afterwards in Outlook or webmail, and that rule decides the implementation: reading never marks a message as read, a send files exactly one copy in Sent, a delete moves to Trash, a draft is saved where another client can edit it, a move keeps flags and the internal date, and folders resolve by their special-use flag instead of by name. It archives and reports spam by role rather than by folder name, so on Gmail, with no archive folder, archiving drops the inbox label. It reads attachments: a PDF, a Word file or a spreadsheet as text, a photo as a picture. After a send, check_bounces says whether an address failed permanently or is still being retried, and check_receipts whether it was opened, even when the honest answer is that nothing came back. A diary connected as a separate step adds calendar tools: reading and searching events, free/busy, booking and moving your own time, inviting, cancelling, answering or proposing another time, and the out-of-office reply. A CardDAV address book connected to an IMAP mailbox, also separately, lets find_contact read the book beside the mailbox's own history, labelling each result's source, and adds read_contact to open one card. No contact is ever stored on the server. A mailbox with no diary or book is handed none of those tools rather than tools that refuse, so the tool count varies by mailbox.
com.mailbox-mcp.toolsNote: This list is the mail surface, which every connected mailbox gets. The calendar and contact tools are absent: each is registered only on a mailbox whose owner has connected a diary or an address book, and Outlook contacts on a Microsoft mailbox that reconnects, so listing them here would be a promise the server had not kept. find_contact is listed because every mailbox has it; a connected book improves it, and a writable one makes the contact tools five. The summary says what each adds.
worksWith: Any IMAP and SMTP mail host
Microsoft 365 and Exchange Online, over OAuth
Gmail and Google Workspace, with an app password
Microsoft 365 and Google calendars, over OAuth

server.name: io.form/formio-mcp
server.description: Create and manage Form.io forms, resources, actions, roles, and projects from your AI agent.

environmentVariables.description: Optional, and the WEAKEST of the three project sources: a committed formio.json found by walking up from the working directory wins, then the per-directory mapping project_set writes, then this. It pins nothing — project_set can redirect a directory whose environment names a different project. Useful for a launch with nowhere to record a project, such as CI or a container (e.g. https://examples.form.io on the hosted cloud; self-hosted it is either https://your-project.your-domain.com or https://your-host/project-name, depending on how that deployment routes projects). Leave it unset and the agent asks for a project and records it per directory.
environmentVariables.name: FORMIO_PROJECT_URL

environmentVariables.description: Optional, and usually unnecessary: the base URL is DERIVED from the project URL — https://api.form.io for a project on a form.io host, the parent path for a project addressed as a sub-directory — and is asked for only when it cannot be derived, which is a path-less project URL on a customer domain. There is no default. Like FORMIO_PROJECT_URL it is the weakest source, behind a committed formio.json and the per-directory mapping.
environmentVariables.name: FORMIO_BASE_URL

environmentVariables.description: Form.io project API key. Optional — when omitted the server uses a browser-based portal login flow to obtain a JWT.
environmentVariables.name: FORMIO_API_KEY

environmentVariables.description: URL of a custom login form used by the browser-based portal login flow. Defaults to the deployment's portal login form.
environmentVariables.name: FORMIO_LOGIN_FORM

environmentVariables.description: Set to 1 to attempt the browser login even where the server detects it cannot present one (CI, a container, a remote shell with no display). Use it when the login page is reachable from a browser elsewhere.
environmentVariables.name: FORMIO_FORCE_BROWSER

environmentVariables.description: Set to 1 to skip TLS certificate verification. For local development against self-signed certificates only — never enable in production.
environmentVariables.name: FORMIO_INSECURE_TLS

server.name: io.github.Sofiia7/actually
server.description: Matches news to Polymarket markets and returns the market's probability. Optional capped trading.

environmentVariables.description: Optional. Your own Polygon EOA private key. Enables the trading tools (place_order, sell_order, cancel_order, get_open_orders, get_positions). Omit to run signal-only, which needs no key and no wallet.
environmentVariables.name: POLYMARKET_PRIVATE_KEY

environmentVariables.description: Optional. Per-order USD cap for the trading tools (default 100). Enforced server-side against the market's own price, so a caller cannot understate an order to slip past it.
environmentVariables.name: ACTUALLY_MAX_ORDER_USD

environmentVariables.description: Optional. Rolling UTC-day USD cap shared by place_order and sell_order (default 500). Held in a persisted ledger, so it survives restarts.
environmentVariables.name: ACTUALLY_DAILY_LIMIT_USD

environmentVariables.description: Optional. Set to exactly 'true' to additionally register redeem_position. A second opt-in beyond the private key, because it submits a real on-chain transaction through Polymarket's relayer and is still in testing.
environmentVariables.name: ACTUALLY_ENABLE_REDEEM

environmentVariables.description: Optional. Set to exactly 'true' to let check_news fall back to Polymarket's own market search when nothing in the cached set matches. Off by default: the query is built from the caller's text and leaves the machine.
environmentVariables.name: ACTUALLY_SEARCH_FALLBACK

environmentVariables.description: Optional. Where the spend ledger is stored (default ~/.actually-mcp-server/spend-guard.json).
environmentVariables.name: ACTUALLY_SPEND_STATE_PATH

environmentVariables.description: Optional. Only if you run your own Cloudflare Worker instead of the shared default.
environmentVariables.name: ACTUALLY_WORKER_URL

environmentVariables.description: Optional. Shared secret for your own Worker. Not a private credential: the default one ships inside every client by design.
environmentVariables.name: ACTUALLY_WORKER_SECRET

server.description: Put an AI agent to work for USDC, or let it hire: take and post on-chain bounties, get paid.
server.title: ArcBounty

environmentVariables.description: Which chain this instance serves: "arc-testnet" (default), "base-mainnet", "base-sepolia" or "arc-mainnet". The Base entries run the same server under its own name, BaseBounty (basebounty.app), with every address baked in. "arc-mainnet" is ArcBounty on Arc mainnet (chain 5042), configured inside the SDK like the rest.
environmentVariables.name: ARC_NETWORK

environmentVariables.description: Optional BountyAdapter override, testnets only. Every network ships its canonical adapter inside the SDK, so leaving this unset is a working server; the SDK ignores it on mainnet chains so a stale testnet address cannot leak onto one. Addresses: contracts/DEPLOYMENTS.md in the repo.
environmentVariables.name: BOUNTY_ADAPTER_ADDRESS

environmentVariables.description: RPC URL override for the resolved network, whichever it is. Defaults to that network public endpoint if unset.
environmentVariables.name: ARC_RPC_URL

environmentVariables.description: Raw private key of the agent wallet. Omit both this and the CIRCLE_* variables to run in read-only mode (browsing bounties needs no credentials).
environmentVariables.name: AGENT_PRIVATE_KEY

environmentVariables.description: Circle Developer-Controlled Wallet API key - alternative to AGENT_PRIVATE_KEY, no raw key in this process.
environmentVariables.name: CIRCLE_API_KEY

environmentVariables.description: Circle Developer-Controlled Wallet entity secret.
environmentVariables.name: ENTITY_SECRET

environmentVariables.description: Circle Developer-Controlled Wallet ID.
environmentVariables.name: CIRCLE_WALLET_ID

environmentVariables.description: Circle Developer-Controlled Wallet address.
environmentVariables.name: CIRCLE_WALLET_ADDRESS

environmentVariables.description: Optional, default 20. The largest reward post_bounty accepts for one bounty, in USDC.
environmentVariables.name: ARCBOUNTY_MAX_REWARD_USDC

environmentVariables.description: Optional, default 50. The most post_bounty posts in total during one run of the server, in USDC.
environmentVariables.name: ARCBOUNTY_MAX_SPEND_USDC

server.description: Standalone MCP server for Obsidian vaults — hybrid search, notes & files, memory, tasks, OAuth 2.1
server.title: Vault Cortex

headers.description: Bearer token used by the MCP client. Must match the MCP_AUTH_TOKEN env var passed to the container.

MCP_AUTH_TOKEN.description: Bearer token for MCP client authentication. Generate with: openssl rand -hex 32

headers.name: Authorization

runtimeArguments.description: Publish the container's port 8000 on the host.
runtimeArguments.name: -p

runtimeArguments.description: Bind-mount your Obsidian vault into the container at /vault.

VAULT_PATH.description: Absolute path to your Obsidian vault on the host machine.

runtimeArguments.name: -v

runtimeArguments.description: Named volume for persistent state under /data — search index, OAuth token DB, and any log files. Keeps OAuth sessions alive across container restarts.
runtimeArguments.name: -v

environmentVariables.description: Bearer token for MCP client authentication. Must match the Authorization header sent by clients. Generate with: openssl rand -hex 32
environmentVariables.name: MCP_AUTH_TOKEN

environmentVariables.description: Public URL clients use to reach this server. Used as the OAuth issuer URL in discovery metadata. Override when exposing the server outside localhost or on a non-default port.
environmentVariables.name: PUBLIC_URL

environmentVariables.description: Enable or disable the embedding pipeline. When false, no ONNX model is downloaded, no vector tables are created, and search uses FTS5 only.
environmentVariables.name: EMBEDDING_ENABLED

environmentVariables.description: Cross-encoder reranking mode: blended (position-aware score blending after RRF fusion) or none (skip reranking). Only takes effect when EMBEDDING_ENABLED is true.
environmentVariables.name: RERANK_MODE

environmentVariables.description: Windows bind-mount mode: enables filesystem polling for the file watcher and rename-based moves across the Docker Desktop/WSL2 bridge. Set to true when the vault lives on a Windows drive.
environmentVariables.name: WINDOWS_MODE

environmentVariables.description: Enable or disable the structured memory layer. When false, memory tools are hidden, bootstrap is skipped, and server metadata omits memory references.
environmentVariables.name: MEMORY_ENABLED

environmentVariables.description: Enable or disable file tools (vault_read_file, vault_list_files). When false, file tools are hidden and server metadata omits file tool references.
environmentVariables.name: FILE_TOOLS_ENABLED

environmentVariables.description: Run the server read-only: every vault-writing tool is hidden, the memory folder is not auto-created, and server metadata omits write references.
environmentVariables.name: READONLY_MODE

environmentVariables.description: Hide individual tools by name, comma-separated. Subtractive only — it cannot re-enable a tool another setting hides; an unknown tool name stops the server at startup.
environmentVariables.name: DISABLED_TOOLS

environmentVariables.description: Vault folder for structured memory files (About Me-style notes). Memory tools are hidden when MEMORY_ENABLED is false, but this value still feeds the defaults for PROTECTED_PATHS and ORPHAN_EXCLUDE_FOLDERS.
environmentVariables.name: MEMORY_DIR

environmentVariables.description: Vault folder for daily notes. Overrides the folder configured in Obsidian's daily-notes plugin. When unset, read from the vault's .obsidian/daily-notes.json, falling back to "Daily Notes".
environmentVariables.name: DAILY_NOTES_FOLDER

environmentVariables.description: Filename date format for daily notes (Moment.js tokens). Overrides the format configured in Obsidian's daily-notes plugin. When unset, read from the vault's .obsidian/daily-notes.json, falling back to "YYYY-MM-DD".
environmentVariables.name: DAILY_NOTES_FORMAT

environmentVariables.description: Number of trusted reverse-proxy hops used to derive the client IP from X-Forwarded-For for OAuth rate limiting and request logs. With 0, injected forwarding headers are ignored.
environmentVariables.name: TRUST_PROXY_HOPS

environmentVariables.description: How many entries from the end of the RFC 7239 Forwarded header's for= list to count to reach the client IP for OAuth rate limiting and request logs. 0 ignores the header; 1 when the proxy in front writes it (e.g. AWS API Gateway); 2 when a CDN fronts that proxy and is the only way to reach it.
environmentVariables.name: TRUST_FORWARDED_HOPS

environmentVariables.description: IANA timezone for timestamps and daily note resolution.
environmentVariables.name: TZ

environmentVariables.description: Logging verbosity.
environmentVariables.name: LOG_LEVEL

environmentVariables.description: Directory for log files that survive container re-creation. The container's own log is always written but discarded when the container is recreated; date-stamped files under LOG_DIR persist on the data volume. Default: /data/logs (remote image), $STORAGE_ROOT/data/logs (single-volume mode), none (local image). none keeps only the container log.
environmentVariables.name: LOG_DIR

environmentVariables.description: Days to keep log files before automatic cleanup on startup; only applies when LOG_DIR is a path.
environmentVariables.name: LOG_RETENTION_DAYS

environmentVariables.description: Comma-separated vault folder names blocked from vault_delete_note and vault_move_note. Default: MEMORY_DIR plus the daily notes folder, read from DAILY_NOTES_FOLDER or .obsidian/daily-notes.json (default Daily Notes). When set, overrides the default entirely.
environmentVariables.name: PROTECTED_PATHS

environmentVariables.description: Comma-separated vault folder names excluded from vault_find_orphans. Default: DAILY_NOTES_FOLDER (else "Daily Notes"), "Templates", MEMORY_DIR.
environmentVariables.name: ORPHAN_EXCLUDE_FOLDERS

environmentVariables.description: Override the OAuth service documentation URL exposed via discovery metadata.
environmentVariables.name: SERVICE_DOCUMENTATION_URL

environmentVariables.description: Largest file vault_read_file will read, in bytes. Reading a larger file returns an error instead of content.
environmentVariables.name: MAX_FILE_BYTES

environmentVariables.description: Byte budget for images returned by vault_read_file, in binary bytes before base64 encoding. Images exceeding the budget are downscaled/recompressed server-side to fit; raise for clients that accept larger tool responses.
environmentVariables.name: MAX_IMAGE_OUTPUT_BYTES

environmentVariables.description: Maximum PDF pages to render as images when raw: true is set on vault_read_file. The per-page byte budget is MAX_IMAGE_OUTPUT_BYTES divided evenly across the rendered pages.
environmentVariables.name: MAX_PDF_RENDER_PAGES

headers.description: Bearer token used by the MCP client. Must match the MCP_AUTH_TOKEN env var passed to the container.

MCP_AUTH_TOKEN.description: Bearer token for MCP client authentication. Generate with: openssl rand -hex 32

headers.name: Authorization

runtimeArguments.description: Publish the container's port 8000 on the host.
runtimeArguments.name: -p

runtimeArguments.description: Bind-mount your Obsidian vault into the container at /vault.

VAULT_PATH.description: Absolute path to your Obsidian vault on the host machine.

runtimeArguments.name: -v

runtimeArguments.description: Named volume for persistent state under /data — search index, OAuth token DB, and any log files. Keeps OAuth sessions alive across container restarts.
runtimeArguments.name: -v

environmentVariables.description: Bearer token for MCP client authentication. Must match the Authorization header sent by clients. Generate with: openssl rand -hex 32
environmentVariables.name: MCP_AUTH_TOKEN

environmentVariables.description: Public URL clients use to reach this server. Used as the OAuth issuer URL in discovery metadata. Override when exposing the server outside localhost or on a non-default port.
environmentVariables.name: PUBLIC_URL

environmentVariables.description: Enable or disable the embedding pipeline. When false, no ONNX model is downloaded, no vector tables are created, and search uses FTS5 only.
environmentVariables.name: EMBEDDING_ENABLED

environmentVariables.description: Cross-encoder reranking mode: blended (position-aware score blending after RRF fusion) or none (skip reranking). Only takes effect when EMBEDDING_ENABLED is true.
environmentVariables.name: RERANK_MODE

environmentVariables.description: Windows bind-mount mode: enables filesystem polling for the file watcher and rename-based moves across the Docker Desktop/WSL2 bridge. Set to true when the vault lives on a Windows drive.
environmentVariables.name: WINDOWS_MODE

environmentVariables.description: Enable or disable the structured memory layer. When false, memory tools are hidden, bootstrap is skipped, and server metadata omits memory references.
environmentVariables.name: MEMORY_ENABLED

environmentVariables.description: Enable or disable file tools (vault_read_file, vault_list_files). When false, file tools are hidden and server metadata omits file tool references.
environmentVariables.name: FILE_TOOLS_ENABLED

environmentVariables.description: Run the server read-only: every vault-writing tool is hidden, the memory folder is not auto-created, and server metadata omits write references.
environmentVariables.name: READONLY_MODE

environmentVariables.description: Hide individual tools by name, comma-separated. Subtractive only — it cannot re-enable a tool another setting hides; an unknown tool name stops the server at startup.
environmentVariables.name: DISABLED_TOOLS

environmentVariables.description: Vault folder for structured memory files (About Me-style notes). Memory tools are hidden when MEMORY_ENABLED is false, but this value still feeds the defaults for PROTECTED_PATHS and ORPHAN_EXCLUDE_FOLDERS.
environmentVariables.name: MEMORY_DIR

environmentVariables.description: Vault folder for daily notes. Overrides the folder configured in Obsidian's daily-notes plugin. When unset, read from the vault's .obsidian/daily-notes.json, falling back to "Daily Notes".
environmentVariables.name: DAILY_NOTES_FOLDER

environmentVariables.description: Filename date format for daily notes (Moment.js tokens). Overrides the format configured in Obsidian's daily-notes plugin. When unset, read from the vault's .obsidian/daily-notes.json, falling back to "YYYY-MM-DD".
environmentVariables.name: DAILY_NOTES_FORMAT

environmentVariables.description: Number of trusted reverse-proxy hops used to derive the client IP from X-Forwarded-For for OAuth rate limiting and request logs. With 0, injected forwarding headers are ignored.
environmentVariables.name: TRUST_PROXY_HOPS

environmentVariables.description: How many entries from the end of the RFC 7239 Forwarded header's for= list to count to reach the client IP for OAuth rate limiting and request logs. 0 ignores the header; 1 when the proxy in front writes it (e.g. AWS API Gateway); 2 when a CDN fronts that proxy and is the only way to reach it.
environmentVariables.name: TRUST_FORWARDED_HOPS

environmentVariables.description: IANA timezone for timestamps and daily note resolution.
environmentVariables.name: TZ

environmentVariables.description: Logging verbosity.
environmentVariables.name: LOG_LEVEL

environmentVariables.description: Directory for log files that survive container re-creation. The container's own log is always written but discarded when the container is recreated; date-stamped files under LOG_DIR persist on the data volume. Default: /data/logs (remote image), $STORAGE_ROOT/data/logs (single-volume mode), none (local image). none keeps only the container log.
environmentVariables.name: LOG_DIR

environmentVariables.description: Days to keep log files before automatic cleanup on startup; only applies when LOG_DIR is a path.
environmentVariables.name: LOG_RETENTION_DAYS

environmentVariables.description: Comma-separated vault folder names blocked from vault_delete_note and vault_move_note. Default: MEMORY_DIR plus the daily notes folder, read from DAILY_NOTES_FOLDER or .obsidian/daily-notes.json (default Daily Notes). When set, overrides the default entirely.
environmentVariables.name: PROTECTED_PATHS

environmentVariables.description: Comma-separated vault folder names excluded from vault_find_orphans. Default: DAILY_NOTES_FOLDER (else "Daily Notes"), "Templates", MEMORY_DIR.
environmentVariables.name: ORPHAN_EXCLUDE_FOLDERS

environmentVariables.description: Override the OAuth service documentation URL exposed via discovery metadata.
environmentVariables.name: SERVICE_DOCUMENTATION_URL

environmentVariables.description: Largest file vault_read_file will read, in bytes. Reading a larger file returns an error instead of content.
environmentVariables.name: MAX_FILE_BYTES

environmentVariables.description: Byte budget for images returned by vault_read_file, in binary bytes before base64 encoding. Images exceeding the budget are downscaled/recompressed server-side to fit; raise for clients that accept larger tool responses.
environmentVariables.name: MAX_IMAGE_OUTPUT_BYTES

environmentVariables.description: Maximum PDF pages to render as images when raw: true is set on vault_read_file. The per-page byte budget is MAX_IMAGE_OUTPUT_BYTES divided evenly across the rendered pages.
environmentVariables.name: MAX_PDF_RENDER_PAGES

environmentVariables.description: API key for higher rate limits. An agent can issue itself one with the zerodust_register_api_key tool, with no human signup step.

environmentVariables.description: Set to "true" to enable the sweep tools. Sweeping moves real funds, so it is off by default and also requires one of the four signing-key variables below.

environmentVariables.description: Path or specifier of a module whose default export returns a viem LocalAccount. This is how Turnkey, Privy, AWS KMS or any other custody service is used, without a raw key ever reaching this server. Preferred over ZERODUST_PRIVATE_KEY.

environmentVariables.description: Path to an encrypted V3 keystore (as produced by `cast wallet import` or geth). Requires ZERODUST_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD_FILE or ZERODUST_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD.
environmentVariables.name: ZERODUST_KEYSTORE_FILE

environmentVariables.description: Path to a file containing the keystore password, so the password never enters the MCP config.
environmentVariables.name: ZERODUST_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD_FILE

environmentVariables.description: Keystore password inline. Prefer ZERODUST_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD_FILE.
environmentVariables.name: ZERODUST_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD

environmentVariables.description: Path to a file containing a hex private key, so the key stays out of the MCP config.
environmentVariables.name: ZERODUST_PRIVATE_KEY_FILE

environmentVariables.description: Private key for the agent's own wallet, inline. Used locally to sign the EIP-7702 authorization and EIP-712 sweep intent; never transmitted, only the resulting signatures are sent. The signer-module, keystore and key-file options above keep it out of your config entirely.
environmentVariables.name: ZERODUST_PRIVATE_KEY

environmentVariables.description: Comma-separated allowlist of sweep destinations. When unset, funds can only be swept to the agent's own address.
environmentVariables.name: ZERODUST_ALLOWED_DESTINATIONS

environmentVariables.name: APPLE_MUSIC_USER_TOKEN

environmentVariables.name: APPLE_MUSIC_WEB_USER_TOKEN

environmentVariables.description: Optional override for the web-player developer token (normally read automatically from music.apple.com).
environmentVariables.name: APPLE_MUSIC_WEB_DEVELOPER_TOKEN

environmentVariables.description: Two-letter Apple Music storefront (e.g. us, gb). Default: your account's storefront, else us.
environmentVariables.name: APPLE_MUSIC_STOREFRONT

environmentVariables.name: ICLOUD_USERNAME

environmentVariables.description: An app-specific password from appleid.apple.com → Sign-In and Security → App-Specific Passwords (NOT your Apple ID password).
environmentVariables.name: ICLOUD_APP_PASSWORD

environmentVariables.description: Your @icloud.com address, only if your Apple ID email is not an iCloud address (needed for Mail).
environmentVariables.name: ICLOUD_MAIL_ADDRESS

environmentVariables.description: Calendar new events go to when none is named (default: the first writable event calendar).
environmentVariables.name: ICLOUD_DEFAULT_CALENDAR

environmentVariables.description: "none" = read-only tools; "additive" = also create/append, never modify, delete or send; "all" = everything (default). Unrecognized values fail closed to "none".

environmentVariables.description: Comma-separated services to enable (music, calendar, contacts, mail, maps, weather, itunes). Default: all.
environmentVariables.name: APPLE_SERVICES

environmentVariables.description: IANA time zone (e.g. America/New_York) for displayed times and for dates you give without an offset. Set this on a hosted server, which runs in UTC.
environmentVariables.name: DISPLAY_TZ

environmentVariables.description: "metric" (default) or "imperial" units for weather (Maps distances always show both).
environmentVariables.name: APPLE_UNITS

environmentVariables.description: Set to false to write nothing under $MCP_DATA_DIR/.apple-icloud-mcp: no web-player token or iCloud discovery cache, and the rejected-password latch and spent confirmation tokens then last only as long as the process.
environmentVariables.name: APPLE_STATE_CACHE

environmentVariables.description: Per-request timeout in milliseconds (default 30000).
environmentVariables.name: APPLE_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS

environmentVariables.description: Set to 1 to log every upstream request line to stderr (credentials redacted).
environmentVariables.name: APPLE_DEBUG_LOG

environmentVariables.description: How confirm-gated writes (send mail, deletes, removing tracks, invitations) behave on a client with no prompt, like claude.ai: "ask-user" (default: preview + confirmToken, the model must get your OK), "auto", or "refuse". Unknown values mean refuse.

environmentVariables.description: Lifetime of a confirmToken in seconds (default 600).
environmentVariables.name: MCP_CONFIRM_TTL_SECONDS

environmentVariables.description: Signing key for confirmTokens. Random per process by default; set it so a token issued just before a restart or redeploy still works (spent tokens are recorded on disk, so none can be replayed).

server.name: io.github.chrischall/ofw-mcp
server.description: OurFamilyWizard co-parenting for Claude — messages, calendar, expenses, and journal

environmentVariables.description: Your OurFamilyWizard login email address. Optional — if omitted, the server falls back to the fetchproxy browser extension (requires being signed in to ourfamilywizard.com).
environmentVariables.name: OFW_USERNAME

environmentVariables.description: Your OurFamilyWizard password. Optional — see OFW_USERNAME.
environmentVariables.name: OFW_PASSWORD

environmentVariables.description: Write-tool gate: "none" registers no write tools; "drafts" registers draft-level writes only (save/delete drafts, upload attachments); "all" registers everything (default). Unrecognized values fail closed to "none".
environmentVariables.name: OFW_WRITE_MODE

environmentVariables.description: Set to "true" to register calendar write tools (create/update/delete event) in "drafts" write mode. Events have no draft stage but are reversible. Never overrides "none".
environmentVariables.name: OFW_CALENDAR_WRITES

environmentVariables.description: Default "true". Set "false" to forbid any tool from marking a message read on OurFamilyWizard - reading a body for the first time stamps a co-parent-visible "First Viewed" time that cannot be undone. A ceiling: no per-call argument can raise it.
environmentVariables.name: OFW_ALLOW_MARK_READ

environmentVariables.description: Default "false". Whether ofw_sync_messages fetches unread inbox bodies by default (each fetch stamps a First Viewed time). Capped by OFW_ALLOW_MARK_READ.
environmentVariables.name: OFW_FETCH_UNREAD_BODIES

environmentVariables.description: Set to false to disable the on-disk session cache and re-authenticate on every process start. Defaults to enabled.
environmentVariables.name: OFW_SESSION_CACHE

environmentVariables.description: Absolute path for the session cache file. Defaults to $MCP_DATA_DIR/.ofw-mcp/session.json.
environmentVariables.name: OFW_SESSION_FILE

server.name: io.github.chrischall/resy-mcp
server.description: Resy reservation management — search, book, cancel, favorites, and Priority Notify for Claude

environmentVariables.description: Your Resy account email. Optional — leave unset to use the fetchproxy browser bridge instead.
environmentVariables.name: RESY_EMAIL

environmentVariables.description: Your Resy account password. Optional — leave unset to use the fetchproxy browser bridge instead.
environmentVariables.name: RESY_PASSWORD

environmentVariables.description: Pre-obtained x-resy-auth-token. Overrides email/password and the fetchproxy bridge. Power users / CI only.
environmentVariables.name: RESY_AUTH_TOKEN

environmentVariables.description: Set to '1' to disable the fetchproxy fallback (forces RESY_EMAIL+PASSWORD or RESY_AUTH_TOKEN).
environmentVariables.name: RESY_DISABLE_FETCHPROXY

environmentVariables.description: Pin the api key, beating both the key captured from the live site and the compiled-in default. Rotation does not require it: the key is captured and cached automatically.
environmentVariables.name: RESY_API_KEY

environmentVariables.description: Set to false to disable the on-disk token cache and re-authenticate on every process start. Defaults to enabled.
environmentVariables.name: RESY_TOKEN_CACHE

environmentVariables.description: Absolute path for the token cache file. Defaults to $MCP_DATA_DIR/.resy-mcp/token.json.
environmentVariables.name: RESY_TOKEN_FILE

environmentVariables.description: Absolute path for the api-key cache file. Defaults to $MCP_DATA_DIR/.resy-mcp/api-key.json. Holds the bare key captured from the live site, which takes precedence over the compiled-in default.
environmentVariables.name: RESY_API_KEY_FILE

environmentVariables.description: Seconds to wait for the signed-in page to make an API call the bridge can read the auth token from. Defaults to 30. Capture resolves on the next matching request, so an idle tab needs a longer window than a busy one.
environmentVariables.name: RESY_CAPTURE_TIMEOUT

environmentVariables.description: Port for the fetchproxy bridge. The whole fleet shares 37149 (the Transporter extension dials it), so override only for local development, test isolation, or a hosted bridged registration — this is the variable to name in the registration's bridgePortEnv.
environmentVariables.name: RESY_WS_PORT

environmentVariables.description: Set to 1 to run every client-side validation and return the request that would have been sent, without sending it or acquiring a token.

environmentVariables.description: Lifetime ceiling across all payments, in atomic units. Required for the same reason as the per-request cap.

environmentVariables.description: Comma-separated hosts that may be paid. Anything else is refused however convincing the challenge looks.

environmentVariables.description: Networks to accept. Defaults to base.

environmentVariables.description: Override for the public origin when a proxy rewrites Host. Must exactly match the URL entered in the client.

environmentVariables.description: Explicit trusted-network-only escape hatch for HTTP mode. Never enable on a public interface.

server.description: One searchable history across every AI coding tool, with secret scanning and a shared task board.

environmentVariables.description: Server to sync to. Defaults to the hosted service at https://chatrecall.dev; set it to your own instance to self-host. Self-hosting is free for one person.
environmentVariables.name: CHAT_RECALL_SERVER

environmentVariables.description: Which tools to register: "lean" (default, 28 tools — tool choice degrades as the list grows) or "full" (all 63 tools, plus recall_help — a directory of the rest; 4 code-intelligence tools register only with the codeindex companion on PATH). Every tool works when called by name either way.
environmentVariables.name: CHAT_RECALL_MCP_PROFILE

environmentVariables.description: Set to 1 to load the whole server inside each session. By default every session with the same profile and server shares one background daemon, and each session is a thin relay onto it — the engine is loaded once per machine instead of once per session. Turn it off for a sandbox with no writable runtime directory.
environmentVariables.name: CHAT_RECALL_NO_DAEMON

environmentVariables.description: Seconds with no session attached before the shared daemon exits and returns its memory. Default 900. Set 0 to keep it resident.
environmentVariables.name: CHAT_RECALL_DAEMON_IDLE_SECS

environmentVariables.description: Compute context that backs SAS code execution.

environmentVariables.description: Expose only tools that neither change server-side state nor cause server-side work (51 of 92). Composes with MCP_TIERS.

environmentVariables.name: MCP_STATELESS_HTTP

io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.summary: Tersign is the evidence layer for agent commerce (B2B / machine-to-machine). Agents issue seller-signed EIP-712 receipts and action records; the hosted ledger at https://tersign.ai optionally counter-signs them into per-seller hash chains that anyone can verify without an account. Disputes export as venue-ready evidence envelopes (generic / internet-court / kleros / uma). The SDK and MCP server work fully standalone without the hosted ledger: issue and verify offline, counter-sign later. Record shapes are pinned by public conformance vectors: https://github.com/tersignhq/evidence-record-conformance (Apache-2.0, CI-tested). Verify a live counter-signed record right now: npx tersign verify 0xe5874f1ffe87f0a6dd9eb157730f67b86ee4538b125fe30fcc4e165213dd3fc4 --ledger https://tersign.ai

io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.summary: Tersign is the evidence layer for agent commerce (B2B / machine-to-machine). Agents issue seller-signed EIP-712 receipts and action records; the hosted ledger at https://tersign.ai optionally counter-signs them into per-seller hash chains that anyone can verify without an account. Disputes export as venue-ready evidence envelopes (generic / internet-court / kleros / uma). The SDK and MCP server work fully standalone without the hosted ledger: issue and verify offline, counter-sign later. No configuration is needed: every environment variable is optional, and the server generates and keeps a local signing key on first run when none is set. record_disclosure's first call self-provisions a free signer-keyed account on the ledger (https://tersign.ai by default), except when that key is already registered to an API-key account (409) or the daily provisioning caps are reached (429; https://tersign.ai/pricing). Record shapes are pinned by public conformance vectors: https://github.com/tersignhq/evidence-record-conformance (Apache-2.0, CI-tested). Verify a live counter-signed record right now: npx tersign verify 0xe5874f1ffe87f0a6dd9eb157730f67b86ee4538b125fe30fcc4e165213dd3fc4 --ledger https://tersign.ai
